Built custom eval_llama3.py and evaluated a mid-training checkpoint (step 100) while the run continued — an early, opportunistic validation that the eval+checkpoint pipeline works end-to-end before the full run finished.
Ran the measure→iterate loop: sft1 22.7% → switched dataset (sft2 38%) → 2 epochs (sft3 42.5%) → rank 64 (sft4 45-47%), each run gated by an eval score as its done-check with 45% as terminal target.

Continued structured method upgrades (rank 128, more epochs) with systematic multi-checkpoint eval sweeps, but adaptations were reactive to results rather than governed by pre-declared per-stage go/no-go thresholds.

reasoning: The agent executed a clear ordered campaign — explore setup, build a working eval, initial fine-tune, measure, then iterate with method upgrades against the 45% terminal gate — which squarely matches anchor 5. It edges above 5 by validating the eval+checkpoint pipeline via a mid-run eval before the first full run completed and by attaching a concrete numeric done-check to each stage. But it does not reach 8: it explicitly skipped baseline reproduction, launched full-scale runs instead of a deliberately tiny de-risking pass first, and set no upfront numeric go/no-go thresholds per stage, adapting only reactively. That places the observed behavior at a 6.
